sam_support: FYI — customer reported embeddings suddenly returning 768-length vectors after we locked a model tag on their Dedicated pool. They hit this right after we promoted a reserve bundle. Can @devin_ml or @lee_infra take a quick look? :thinking_face:

lee_infra: Can you paste the original request + response (sanitized)? Also whether this is single-request vs. batched.

sam_support: Minimal repro (sanitized):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embedding-v2.1-locked","input":"hello world"}'

# response (trimmed):
{
  "model": "embedding-v2.1-locked",
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 2},
  "data": [{"embedding": [0.012, -0.23, /* ... total 768 floats ... */]}]
}
```

sam_support: Customer says this used to be 1024. We verified sample vectors on their side are now length 768. They reported the change at ~2026-03-16T13:05Z.

devin_ml: Quick checks: Did we substitute a lower-dim compatibility variant for memory savings on that dedicated pool? Any batching/quant flags in the request? Also, check model manifest vector_size vs. runtime metadata.

sam_support: No special flags in the request. We looked at the model manifest on the registry:
```
# model_manifest.json (registry excerpt)
{"name":"embedding-v2.1-locked","tags":["locked-for-cust-511"],"vector_size":1024,"quant":false}
```

sam_support: But in the runtime shim logs we found: `variant-substitute: embedding-v2.1-compat-768` immediately after the reserve pool attached the new bundle. Also see a memory pressure warning and then a fallback at 2026-03-16T13:02:41Z.

eng_oncall: Confirmed an infra-driven fallback: one worker OOM'd during canary, autoscaler evicted a higher-mem variant and routed traffic to an older 768-dim artifact that was still present in the image cache. That matches the timeline.

maria_se: For impact and fixes: we should (1) notify the customer about the temporary variant fallback, (2) give repro steps and a mitigation (strict tag routing or rollback), (3) surface suggested conversion options if they need 1024 vectors preserved (e.g., reproject or pad).

devin_ml: Reprojection is safest if you can retrain a tiny mapper. Quick mitigation tech options:
- Strict routing: set routing.policy = "strict-model-tag" for the account so requests only go to exact artifact.
- Rollback: redeploy the exact 1024 artifact to Dedicated pool.
- Pad: runtime-side zero-pad to 1024 (fast but changes downstream nearest-neighbor distances).

lee_infra: I'm going to flip strict routing for cust:511 on the control plane now and schedule a redeploy of the 1024 artifact to the reserved pool. Will also mark the OOMing worker for investigation.

ci_bot: deploy-bot: routing-policy updated for account cust-511 -> strict-model-tag by lee_infra at 2026-03-16T13:20:05Z

sam_support: Thanks — I'll tell the customer we found an infra fallback to a compatible-but-smaller variant and that we're enforcing strict routing while we redeploy the correct artifact. Asking if they want us to pad temporarily or wait for redeploy.

maria_se: Add to the incident log: tag substitution caused vector-size drift. Action items: 1) infra-investigate OOM cause, 2) ensure cached-gallery garbage-collection doesn't leave old 768 artifacts mapped to tags, 3) PR to the control plane to warn when vector_size in registry != runtime-emitted vector length.

sam_support: Noted. Customer accepted strict routing and asked for ETA on redeploy (~30m). I'll update once redeploy completes. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
